body:
`insight:marks-most-important-thing-2003` | confidence: verified | date: 2003-07-01

Memo of 1 Jul 2003 (later a book). 'The most important thing - above all - is the relationship between price and value.' 'no asset is so good that it can't become a bad investment if bought at too high a price. And there are few assets so bad that they can't be a good investment when bought cheap enough.' On conviction: 'Few things are more dangerous than an incorrect opinion held with conviction and relied on to excess.' Defensive investing: 'If we avoid the losers, the winners will take care of themselves'; ingredients are '(a) insistence on solid, identifiable value at a bargain price, (b) diversification rather than concentration, and (c) avoidance of reliance on macro-forecasts and market timing.' Simplified: 'Invest scared! Worry about the possibility of loss. Worry that there's something you don't know.' Return profile target: 'average in good times ... and far above average in bad times', because 'in the good times, it's good enough to be average.' Other headings (each 'the most important thing'): intrinsic value estimate; avoiding bad years; limits of macro knowledge; 'being mindful of cycles (and where we stand in them)'; contrarian behavior; 'patient opportunism'; 'being leery of leverage'; acknowledging uncontrollable factors. 'Ignoring cycles and extrapolating trends is one of the most dangerous things an investor can do.' Note tension with Buffett's concentration (Marks runs credit); use his loss-avoidance asymmetry rather than his diversification prescription for an equity compounder book.

Sources:
- https://www.oaktreecapital.com/docs/default-source/memos/2003-07-01-the-most-important-thing.pdf

body:
- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:US-OPTU:chapter11-filing-by-jun27`
- **Method:** flags-judgment context · **P(ours)** 0.65 · **P(base)** 0.55 · resolve by 2027-06-30
- **Evidence:** 8-K (16-Nov-2026): CSC Holdings 'elected not to make' ~$102.5m of interest due 16-Nov-2026 on its 11.25% 2028, 4.5% 2031 guaranteed and 5% 2031 notes, entering a 30-day grace period; negotiating with 'the steering committee of an ad hoc group of debtholders' that 'holds the vast majority of the nearly $22 billion of debt'; any deal 'would result in a material reduction of the indebtedness'; 'cannot provide any assurances that such an agreement will be reached within the Grace Period or at all'; cash $1.1bn at 30-Sep-2026. 10-Q (Q2 2026, as restated): going-concern 'substantial doubt' with $4.1225bn principal maturing April 2027 and $2.225bn later in 2027 vs cash $1.30bn; Q2 2026 financials restated for an ASC 740 deferred-tax error (non-reliance), alongside cable-franchise impairments.
- **Why our number differs from base:** Flags-judgment: here the flags (going-concern doubt, skipped coupon, restatement, a $4.1bn April-2027 maturity it cannot pay from cash) all point at the same event and have teeth. With a 'vast majority' ad hoc group already organised, the efficient route to bind holdouts across a ~$22bn multi-tranche structure is usually a pre-packaged or pre-negotiated Chapter 11; an out-of-court exchange is possible but needs near-unanimity. We lean above the reference class.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** Reference class (unverified, from memory of rating-agency default studies): issuers that skip a coupon and enter a grace period while negotiating with an ad hoc group end in a bankruptcy filing within ~6–8 months a bit over half the time; the rest are distressed exchanges or extensions.
- **Resolution rule:** YES if Optimum Communications, Inc., CSC Holdings LLC or any parent/intermediate holding company of CSC Holdings files a voluntary or involuntary petition under Chapter 11 (including a pre-packaged case) on or before 30-Jun-2027, per an 8-K or the bankruptcy docket. A purely out-of-court exchange does not count.
- **Resolution source:** SEC EDGAR 8-K filings of Optimum Communications (CIK 1702780) / PACER or claims-agent docket
- **Sources used:** https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1702780/000170278026000077/optu-20261116.htm; https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=1702780
- **Confidence of evidence:** verified

body:
| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `common.py` | Cache layout, the Indian fiscal calendar, date parsing |
| `fetch.py` | Pulls the NSE announcement list with the short UA `Mozilla/5.0` and filters it to transcript PDFs (catches typos such as "Trancript"; skips .zip files). Downloads **only the PDFs in the date range**, which fixes pilot lesson 1. Runs `pdftotext -layout`, detects the call date (the "held on …" date, never the quarter-end date) and the quarter. Flags PDFs that look scanned (fewer than 1,500 words; these need OCR). |
| `turns.py` | Splits the text into speaker turns: management, analyst, moderator or host. Speaker roles are resolved in this order: (1) the cover-page roster, merged across all of the company's calls, with fuzzy matching (handles "Parmjit Soni", "Paramjit Sonis", "Aditya Dujari :", dropped middle names); (2) generic labels such as "Management:"; (3) analysts named in the moderator's announcement; (4) a content vote. Each turn records `role_basis` so it can be audited. Turns are tagged opening / qa / closing. Removes the cover letter, page headers, safe-harbour text and operator housekeeping. Optional `rosters.json` maps `{SYMBOL: [names]}`. |
| `candidates.py` | Rule-based extraction of forward-looking sentences. Signals: guidance verbs; numbers with %, ₹/INR/cr, tonnes, days; qualitative magnitudes ("mid-teens", "double-digit", "flat"); timelines (FY28, Q3FY27, H2, "next year", "in 2-3 years", "end of the year", month names). A metric may come from the analyst's question when the answer only says "it". Also catches "Yes, absolutely" answers that endorse a target the analyst stated. Output is `candidates.jsonl` with quote, speaker, call date, section, volunteered flag, the question being answered, numbers, and a deadline resolved with the **later-date rule** (`assumed` explains each choice). Tier A = strong, tier B = directional. |
| `llm_extract_prompt.md` | Prompt template for the LLM confirmation and structuring step. The output schema matches `score.py`'s input: measure vocabulary, period, target_low/high, comparator, deadline rules, `chain_key`, `restates_earlier`, `acknowledges_revision`. |
| `llm_extract.py` | Runs the template call by call, oldest first. Feeds the `chain_key`s already used into each later prompt so the same target keeps the same key. Validates the output and assigns ids. Caches raw output in `llm/`. |
| `llm_candour_prompt.md` | Optional per-shortfall prompt: "was this miss admitted unprompted?" |
| `financials.py` | Fetches the screener.in consolidated page with curl (cached for 3 days) and parses the quarterly, P&L, balance-sheet, cash-flow and ratio tables. A CSV can be supplied instead or as an override. |
| `score.py` | Auto-scores financial promises and builds the supersedes chains (details below). |
| `report.py` | MCS, weighted delivery ratio, hit rate, candour index; breakdowns by category, driver (cycle vs execution), specificity, volunteered/prompted, year said and speaker; markdown ledger; memdb seed. |
| `validate.py` | Compares pipeline output with a manual ledger (recall/precision, field agreement, status agreement, goalposts). |
| `run.py` | Orchestrator. |
